s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower urinary tract symptoms with urethral mass and amyloid protein deposition
salient_findings: Nocturia two to three times per night
key_facts: 53-year-old man
3-year history of lower urinary tract symptoms
Nocturia two to three times per night
Slow urinary stream
Microscopic hematuria with 3-5 red cells per high-power field
Normal renal ultrasonography findings
Flexible cystourethroscopy revealed a circumferential urethral mass
Biopsy specimens were negative for carcinoma
Biopsy specimens demonstrated amyloid protein deposition
No history of lichen sclerosis, sexually transmitted infection, pelvic radiation, genitourinary trauma, or family history of genitourinary malignancy
No additional disease manifestations of amyloidosis found on systemic evaluation
Retrograde urethrography showed an approximately 2-cm segment of stenosis in the penile urethra

shortlist.label: Localized amyloidosis of the urethra
shortlist.why_kept: Amyloid protein deposition in urethral mass

shortlist.label: Urethral stricture
shortlist.why_kept: Stenosis in the penile urethra and lower urinary tract symptoms

shortlist.label: Primary amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Amyloid protein deposition without additional disease manifestations

shortlist.label: AL amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible plasma cell dyscrasia with urethral involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a urethral mass with amyloid protein deposition on biopsy, in the absence of systemic amyloidosis manifestations, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Urethral stricture
rejected.why: While the patient has a urethral stenosis, the primary issue is the amyloid deposition, not just a stricture.

rejected.label: Primary amyloidosis
rejected.why: There's no evidence of systemic involvement or other organ dysfunction typical of primary amyloidosis.

rejected.label: AL amyloidosis
rejected.why: No systemic manifestations or evidence of light chain production were mentioned, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Secondary amyloidosis
rejected.why: There's no underlying chronic disease or infection mentioned that would lead to secondary amyloidosis.
